findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify in Scope that 'stale entry' explicitly includes count decrease (actual < pinned), and align AC5 to state 'count increase AND count decrease both fail' so the guard spec and the AC are unambiguous.
evidence: Scope: 'The guard fails on a missing entry, a stale entry, or any count increase'
AC5: 'Tests cover allowlist count drift and stale/vacuous entries'
'stale entry' is undefined — it could mean 'path no longer exists' or 'count changed in either direction'
findings.finding: The Scope section says the guard 'fails on a missing entry, a stale entry, or any count increase,' treating count decrease as a subcase of 'stale entry' without defining staleness. AC5 says tests cover 'count drift,' which implies bidirectional (increase OR decrease) failure. An implementer reading only Scope could reasonably build a guard that catches count increases but treats count decreases as merely stale (possibly with a different exit code or no failure). The two sections do not agree on whether a count decrease is a first-class failure condition identical to a count increase.
scenarios: Implementer builds guard that only errors on count increases, not decreases; a file loses a match (e.g. a carve-out phrase is deleted) but the allowlist still pins the old higher count — guard passes silently instead of failing.
Test author writes a count-decrease injection test expecting non-zero exit, but the guard returns zero because the Scope text only mandates failure on 'count increase.'
findings.suggested_fix: In Scope, replace 'fails on a missing entry, a stale entry, or any count increase' with 'fails on a missing entry, a count mismatch in either direction (actual < pinned or actual > pinned), a duplicate entry, or a path that no longer exists.' Update AC5 to say 'count increase and count decrease' explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the count-pinned exemption data must be a separate `.txt` file or can follow the codebase-standard inline-Python-constants idiom used by all sibling guards (check_dco_identity.py, check_build_env_locked.py, check_verify_gate_parity.py, etc.); if inline constants suffice, eliminate the separate `.txt` config surface.
evidence: check_dco_identity.py lines 19–33: SCOPED_GLOBS, EXCLUDED_PREFIXES, and _PATTERN are all inline Python constants.
check_build_env_locked.py line 33: BASE_ALLOWLIST = {'pip', 'setuptools', 'wheel'} — inline set.
check_verify_gate_parity.py lines 63–72: EXCLUDED_JOBS as inline frozenset with inline justification comments.
No existing scripts/*.txt data file exists in the codebase — the search for 'allowlist.txt' returned no hits.
The allowlist content is a fixed ~15-entry set fully enumerated in the plan's 'Exact-phrase inventory' section — exactly the data shape all sibling guards keep inline.
No AC requires the allowlist to be a separate file; AC1 only requires 'count-pinned, non-vacuous exemptions', which inline Python dicts satisfy.
findings.finding: The plan introduces scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt as a separate plain-text data file for count-pinned exemptions, but every existing sibling guard script in scripts/ (check_dco_identity.py, check_build_env_locked.py, check_docs_index.py, check_verify_gate_parity.py, check_server_manifest.py, check_readme_quickstart.py) stores its bounded, static exemption data as inline Python constants. Externalising the allowlist to a .txt file creates a new config surface with no codebase precedent and no AC-backed justification for why inline constants are insufficient.
findings.location: Scope section: 'Add the plain-text allowlist scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt'; Exact-phrase inventory section
scenarios: A contributor adds a new allowlist entry: they must now understand a custom .txt parse format instead of editing a familiar Python constant.

The parser for .txt format must itself be tested and maintained — the plan's Testing section dedicates entries to 'malformed/duplicate/stale rows', implying bespoke parsing logic that inline constants avoid entirely.
A future guard script author copies the .txt pattern without understanding why, proliferating the config-surface further.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt with an inline Python dict/list in check_criteria_vocabulary.py, following the pattern of EXCLUDED_JOBS in check_verify_gate_parity.py or BASE_ALLOWLIST in check_build_env_locked.py. Each entry can carry a comment for its reason, and count-pinning is naturally expressed as a dict value. This eliminates the bespoke .txt parser, the malformed/duplicate/stale-row failure modes, and aligns with every existing sibling guard.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief rationale in the plan (or a comment in the guard script) explaining why count-pinning requires an external data file rather than an inline Python dict, and how this deliberate divergence from the sibling-script inline-constant convention is justified.
evidence: All 6+ existing sibling scripts (check_build_env_locked.py:33 `BASE_ALLOWLIST = {"pip", "setuptools", "wheel"}`, check_dco_identity.py:26 `EXCLUDED_PREFIXES = (...)`, check_verify_gate_parity.py:63 `EXCLUDED_JOBS = frozenset({...})`) encode their exemption sets as inline Python constants — never as a separate data file.
The plan's 'Exact-phrase inventory and disposition' section lists ~15 allowlisted paths with expected counts — a volume that could fit in a Python dict literal just as readily as a plain-text file.
No prior-art consideration of why an external file is preferable to inline constants is recorded anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a separate plain-text allowlist data file (scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt) for exemptions, diverging from the established pattern used by every sibling guard script in scripts/ — which all encode exemptions as inline Python constants (e.g., BASE_ALLOWLIST in check_build_env_locked.py, EXCLUDED_PREFIXES in check_dco_identity.py, EXCLUDED_JOBS in check_verify_gate_parity.py). The plan does not record why count-pinning requires an external file rather than inline constants, nor does it acknowledge the convention it breaks.
findings.location: Scope section: 'Add the plain-text allowlist scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt. Each non-comment row records a repository-relative path, its expected exact-phrase match count, and a reason.'
scenarios: A future maintainer adds a sibling guard and, following every existing precedent, puts exemptions inline — leaving the vocabulary guard as an unexplained outlier with no recorded rationale.
A reviewer scanning the scripts/ directory sees mixed conventions and cannot tell whether the external-file approach was deliberate (for count-pinning semantics) or accidental.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach section or as an inline comment in check_criteria_vocabulary.py, note: 'The allowlist is an external file rather than inline constants because the count-pinning semantics (each exempted path carries a verified expected occurrence count that fails on drift) would make a Python dict literal grow unbounded and is better expressed as a diffable text file — unlike the binary include/exclude sets used by sibling guards.'
